hero.label: Pardubice → Prague
hero.intro: Pardubice to Prague by private chauffeur is a 110 km door-to-door transfer west on the D11 motorway, around one and a half hours drive time. Prestigo’s fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes-Benz E-Class, fuel and the Czech vignette included. Pickup from any Pardubice address, the main station or Pardubice Airport (PED), drop-off anywhere in Prague.
hero.imageAlt: Private chauffeur transfer from Pardubice to Prague in a Mercedes

openingParagraphs: A private transfer from Pardubice to Prague covers 110 km — north out of the city to join the D11, then west past Poděbrady into Prague — and takes approximately one and a half hours door to door. The fixed fare starts at €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers; groups of up to 6 travel in the V-Class from €{vPrice}; the S-Class is available from €{sPrice} for executive or VIP travel. Your chauffeur collects you at your Pardubice hotel or office, Pardubice main station, the racecourse or Pardubice Airport, and drops you at the door of your Prague hotel, apartment or meeting.

The fare is agreed before you travel and does not move: fuel, the Czech motorway vignette, bottled water, Wi-Fi and child seats on request are all included. Landing at Pardubice and staying in Prague? Your chauffeur is waiting in Arrivals and drives you straight there.

paragraphs: From a pickup on Pernštýnské Square, near the castle or at the main station, your chauffeur leaves Pardubice northbound toward Hradec Králové and joins the D11 motorway. Depending on traffic and where you start, they may take a road west instead to meet the D11 further along — all options are fast, well-signed Czech roads.

Once on the D11 the drive is a straight run west across the Elbe plain, past the spa town of Poděbrady and into Prague through its north-eastern edge. Total distance is approximately 110 kilometres; driving time is about one and a half hours in normal traffic. There is no border on this route — it stays entirely inside the Czech Republic.

Your chauffeur checks the D11 before departure. Weekday evening rush hour and Sunday afternoons slow the final stretch into Prague, and race-day traffic around the Pardubice racecourse is planned for in advance. If there is an accident or roadwork, they reroute without asking.

includedIntro: The fixed price covers everything from your Pardubice pickup to your Prague drop-off: the car, the chauffeur, fuel and the Czech vignette. Flying in to Pardubice, leaving the races or finishing a day of meetings, you step out at your Prague door with nothing left to arrange.
inclusions: A black Mercedes — E-Class, S-Class or V-Class depending on group size and preference. Every vehicle under three years old.
A professional chauffeur — fluent English and Czech. German on request.
Fuel, all tolls and the Czech motorway vignette. Nothing is charged on top.
Pickup at any Pardubice address, Pardubice main station, the racecourse, or inside Arrivals at Pardubice Airport (PED) with flight tracking.
Drop-off at the exact Prague address you give us — hotel entrance, apartment door, office or Václav Havel Airport (PRG).
Bottled water, phone charger and Wi-Fi in the rear cabin.
Child seats on request — rear-facing infant, forward-facing toddler or booster. No additional charge.
Stops on the way — Kunětická hora, Kladruby nad Labem or Poděbrady — agreed at booking.
fleetNote: All vehicles are late-model Mercedes-Benz, maintained to manufacturer standard. Child seats available on request at no charge.

journeyStops.note: Pickup from your hotel, office, the main station, the racecourse or Pardubice Airport (PED). At the airport your chauffeur waits inside Arrivals with your name.
A Gothic castle on a lone hill just north of Pardubice, with views across the East Bohemian plain.
A spa town on the Elbe, just off the D11. A walk along the colonnade before the last half hour to Prague.
A château, a stud farm, a restaurant you have read about? Tell us at booking. The route is yours.
Drop-off at any Prague address, Prague main station or Václav Havel Airport (PRG) for an onward flight.

goodToKnow.label: Border crossing
goodToKnow.value: No border crossing — Pardubice and Prague are both in the Czech Republic.

goodToKnow.label: Tolls
goodToKnow.value: The Czech motorway vignette and any tolls are included in the quoted price.

goodToKnow.label: Airport pickup
goodToKnow.value: Give us your flight number. Your chauffeur tracks the landing at Pardubice Airport and adjusts the pickup time automatically.

goodToKnow.label: Twin cities
goodToKnow.value: Starting in Hradec Králové or visiting both cities? We can cover Pardubice and Hradec Králové in a single booking.

dayTrip.intro: Ninety minutes across East and Central Bohemia passes castles, horses and spa towns. Three stops cover most of the requests we get on the way from Pardubice to Prague.

configurations.title: Kunětická hora Castle
configurations.body: Ten minutes north of Pardubice, the Pernštejn family’s castle sits alone on a volcanic hill. Forty-five minutes on the ramparts and in the courtyard, then on to the D11 and Prague.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: The Kladruby Stud
configurations.body: A short detour west of Pardubice leads to Kladruby nad Labem, the imperial stud farm and its UNESCO-listed landscape, where the grey carriage horses of the old imperial court are still bred. A guided visit takes about an hour.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

configurations.title: Lunch in Poděbrady
configurations.body: Leave the D11 for Poděbrady — a spa town with a riverside château, a long park colonnade and unhurried cafés. An hour for lunch, then thirty minutes into Prague.
configurations.price: Add a stop at booking — contact us for a quote.

dayTrip.footnote: Stops are planned at booking and priced by the extra time and distance — tell us where you would like to stop and we confirm a firm quote before you book. A short coffee or rest stop on the motorway is always included.

chauffeurNarrative: Your chauffeur is at the door when you are ready to leave — your Pardubice hotel, an office in the centre, or inside the Arrivals hall at Pardubice Airport with a name board. Luggage goes straight into the car.

Ninety minutes is enough to work, rest or simply look out of the window. If you would like to know more about Prague before you arrive — your hotel’s neighbourhood, a good table near the river, the easiest way to see the Castle without the crowds — your chauffeur lives there and will tell you.

Water, charger and Wi-Fi are already in the cabin. If you want a coffee on the D11 or a particular temperature in the back, say so. On arrival in Prague your chauffeur carries the bags to reception, not just to the kerb.

items.title: A fare that holds
items.body: Fuel, the Czech vignette and the chauffeur’s time are all included. What you agree at booking is what you pay in Prague.

items.title: Nothing to change
items.body: No transfer from the airport to the station, no platform, no taxi at Praha hlavní nádraží. One car takes you from Pardubice to your Prague door.

items.title: A Prague-based team
items.body: Prestigo operates its own Mercedes fleet from Prague. Your chauffeur knows the city — hotel drop-off points, Old Town restrictions and the quickest way across at rush hour.

faqs.q: How long does a private transfer from Pardubice to Prague take?
faqs.a: Approximately 1 hour 30 minutes door to door: north to the D11 motorway, then west past Poděbrady into Prague. Weekday evening rush hour into Prague can add 10–15 minutes.

faqs.q: How much is a taxi or chauffeur from Pardubice to Prague?
faqs.a: A fixed fare from €{ePrice} in a Mercedes E-Class for up to 3 passengers, €{vPrice} in the V-Class for up to 6, or €{sPrice} in the S-Class. The price includes fuel, the Czech motorway vignette and driver time — it is per car, not per person.

faqs.q: Can you pick me up at Pardubice Airport and drive me to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Give us your flight number when you book. Your chauffeur tracks the landing, waits inside the Arrivals hall at Pardubice Airport with your name, and drives you directly to your Prague address. Up to 60 minutes of waiting at the airport is included.

faqs.q: Is a private transfer better than the train from Pardubice to Prague?
faqs.a: Pardubice is on the main railway line and fast trains reach Prague in about an hour, station to station. For a solo traveller with light luggage the train is the cheaper and sensible choice. A private transfer makes sense for groups, families, heavy luggage or an airport arrival — door to door, at the same price for one passenger or three.

faqs.q: Can we stop on the way from Pardubice to Prague?
faqs.a: Yes. Kunětická hora, the Kladruby stud and Poděbrady are the usual stops. Tell us at booking and we include the stop in a fixed quote. A short coffee or rest break is always included.

faqs.q: Can you collect us from the racecourse after the Velká Pardubická?
faqs.a: Yes. Race day in October brings heavy traffic around the course, so book early and tell us your planned departure time. Your chauffeur agrees a pickup point near the racecourse in advance and drives you straight to Prague.

relatedRoutesIntro: Pardubice is one of several East Bohemian routes into Prague. Clients coming from Hradec Králové, Kutná Hora or Olomouc book the same way — one car, one fixed fare, drop-off at the door in Prague.
